legend: Vasya has a tree consisting of n%%ZSMJ0%% vertices with root in vertex 1%%ZSMJ1%%. At first all vertices has 0%%ZSMJ2%% written on it.

Let d(i,j)%%ZSMJ3%% be the distance between vertices i%%ZSMJ4%% and j%%ZSMJ5%%, i.e. number of edges in the shortest path from i%%ZSMJ6%% to j%%ZSMJ7%%. Also, let's denote k%%ZSMJ8%%-subtree of vertex x%%ZSMJ9%% — set of vertices y%%ZSMJ10%% such that next two conditions are met:
x%%ZSMJ11%% is the ancestor of y%%ZSMJ12%% (each vertex is the ancestor of itself);

Vasya needs you to process m%%ZSMJ14%% queries. The i%%ZSMJ15%%-th query is a triple vi%%ZSMJ16%%, di%%ZSMJ17%% and xi%%ZSMJ18%%. For each query Vasya adds value xi%%ZSMJ19%% to each vertex from di%%ZSMJ20%%-subtree of vi%%ZSMJ21%%.
Report to Vasya all values, written on vertices of the tree after processing all queries.
input: The first line contains single integer n%%ZSMJ22%% (1≤n≤3⋅105%%ZSMJ23%%) — number of vertices in the tree.

Each of next n−1%%ZSMJ24%% lines contains two integers x%%ZSMJ25%% and y%%ZSMJ26%% (1≤x,y≤n%%ZSMJ27%%) — edge between vertices x%%ZSMJ28%% and y%%ZSMJ29%%. It is guarantied that given graph is a tree.
Next line contains single integer m%%ZSMJ30%% (1≤m≤3⋅105%%ZSMJ31%%) — number of queries.
Each of next m%%ZSMJ32%% lines contains three integers vi%%ZSMJ33%%, di%%ZSMJ34%%, xi%%ZSMJ35%% (1≤vi≤n%%ZSMJ36%%, 0≤di≤109%%ZSMJ37%%, 1≤xi≤109%%ZSMJ38%%) — description of the i%%ZSMJ39%%-th query.
output: Print n%%ZSMJ40%% integers. The i%%ZSMJ41%%-th integers is the value, written in the i%%ZSMJ42%%-th vertex after processing all queries.
note: In the first exapmle initial values in vertices are 0,0,0,0,0%%ZSMJ43%%. After the first query values will be equal to 1,1,1,0,0%%ZSMJ44%%. After the second query values will be equal to 1,11,1,0,0%%ZSMJ45%%. After the third query values will be equal to 1,11,1,100,0%%ZSMJ46%%.
